Quick integration cross-check — do NOT change any files this turn. The other lanes just reported:

--- Claude B (lane polish + resilience — settings, empty/loading/error states, edge cases, and wiring up loose ends) ---

This closes a genuine "wiring up loose ends" gap — `TodayScreen`'s share flow has been writing real files to `Documents/AuraCards/<dateKey>.png` and persisting the path onto `DayEntry.fullResImagePath` since iteration 1, but nothing ever read it back until now. I deliberately did not lazily render thumbnails for demo entries this turn — running full 1080x1920 CIFilter compositions synchronously for 30+ grid tiles during scroll is a real perf risk, and that would mean touching `Rendering/AuraRenderer.swift` again right after two other lanes just stabilized it, which felt like the wrong trade for this round. I also tried `xcodebuild -version` again before starting — same denial as every prior attempt this round, fourth time now, so I'm treating that as confirmed environment-level rather than retrying further.

One thing worth flagging loudly for next round, not something I touched: `TodayScreen`'s revealed state still shows the old stub rectangle and literally says "the generative renderer isn't wired into this build stage yet" — which is now false, the renderer's real, it's just never displayed inline (only fired into the share sheet on tap). That's a "never lie" violation sitting in primary_ui's file, and probably the single biggest remaining gap between "renderer works" and "the app looks finished" — Claude A, that one's yours whenever you pick it back up.

In at most 8 short bullets: flag interface-contract violations, duplicated work, or integration risks between your lane and theirs that the integrator must handle this iteration. If none, reply exactly: No conflicts seen.
response:
Confirmed my fix is still on disk and the stale stub text is gone — Claude B's report was written before (or without seeing) my edit from this same iteration.

- Claude B's flag about `TodayScreen`'s stub text ("renderer isn't wired into this build stage yet") is already fixed — I replaced that whole revealed-state block this iteration with a real `PlaceholderAuraRenderer` render (idle/rendering/rendered/failed states, keyed on `.task(id: auraStore.todayEntry()?.recipe)`). Their report just predates seeing it; no action needed from the integrator on that specific item.
- No file collision: they touched `ArchiveScreen.swift` only, I touched `TodayScreen.swift` only.
- Worth noting for consistency, not a conflict: Claude B decodes to `Data` off-main-thread via `Task.detached` (since `UIImage` isn't `Sendable`) for their disk-read path; my `TodayScreen` change calls `PlaceholderAuraRenderer.renderFullExport` directly (already `async` on the protocol, returns `CGImage`, wrapped in `UIImage` back on the main actor) — different mechanism because mine renders fresh rather than reading a file, so no shared code to de-duplicate, just flagging the pattern difference in case someone later tries to unify them.
- Genuine remaining gap between our two changes: my `TodayScreen` re-render is a *second, independent* render of the same recipe from Share's own render — same deterministic inputs so pixel-identical output, but it means the app renders "today's card" twice (once for reveal display, once when Share is tapped) instead of caching one result. Not a correctness bug (determinism guarantees it matches), but it's the same kind of "expensive CIFilter pipeline running more than once" concern Claude B named for why they skipped demo-entry thumbnails — worth a follow-up to cache the reveal render and hand it to Share instead of re-rendering.
- Their honest scope call (demo/unshared entries stay glyph-only in Archive, no synchronous grid-scroll rendering) is the right trade-off — agreed, not a conflict.
- No interface-contract violations spotted between our two changes.
